Yes — there are three more. Five classes implement `Notifier` (defined at `src/notifiers/notifier.ts:8`):

| Class | File |
|---|---|
| `EmailNotifier` | `src/notifiers/emailNotifier.ts:3` |
| `SlackNotifier` | `src/notifiers/slackNotifier.ts:3` |
| `SmsNotifier` | `src/notifiers/smsNotifier.ts:3` |
| `WebhookNotifier` | `src/notifiers/webhookNotifier.ts:3` |
| `ConsoleNotifier` | `src/notifiers/consoleNotifier.ts:3` |

All five are registered in the `notifiers` array at `src/index.ts:12`, so all are live in the dispatch path.

Two things worth knowing if you're planning a change to the interface:

- **Structural implementers count too.** TypeScript interfaces are structural, so anything shaped like `{ notify(event: TaskEvent): void }` satisfies `Notifier` without an `implements` clause. There's one today: the inline fake at `src/scheduler/dispatcher.test.ts:9`. Grepping for `implements Notifier` alone would miss it.
- **The five classes are near-identical in shape.** Each has a public `notify` that delegates to one private helper (`sendText`, `post`, `print`, etc.) which just `console.log`s a prefixed line. So a signature change to `notify` would touch all six sites uniformly.
